answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the cedar check immediately, the vault audit keeps the resolved set and the nebula replay makes public exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 230 aliases as a result pays the reading cost 230 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature.
